title: Chapter 49 — Territory Mapping
intro: The geographic and relationship map that turns random prospecting into systematic business development.

sections.title: Map Before You Prospect
sections.content:
Random cold calling is the least efficient way to build a trade book. Before you pick up the phone, map your territory.

Start with geography. Where are homes being built and renovated in your market? Check building permit data — most municipalities publish it. Drive the neighbourhoods. Where are the construction signs? Where are the dumpsters in driveways? Every permit and every dumpster represents a potential trade account.

Then map the players. Who are the active builders in each area? Who are the designers? Which contractors are doing the most renovations? LinkedIn, local business directories, NKBA and HBA membership lists, and Houzz are all sources.

sections.title: The Opportunity Heat Map
sections.content:
Create a simple spreadsheet or CRM view that maps: builder name, project volume, estimated appliance spend per project, current supplier (if known), and relationship status (unknown, contacted, met, active, won).

This is your pipeline before it becomes a pipeline. The builders doing 20 custom homes per year at $1M+ are your tier-one targets. The renovation contractors doing 50 projects per year are your tier-two. The designers specifying 15 kitchens per year are tier-one regardless of project size because of their specification power.

Prioritize by potential revenue times probability of winning. A $200K annual account with no incumbent relationship is worth more prospecting time than a $500K account locked into a 10-year supplier relationship.

sections.title: Updating the Map
sections.content:
Territory mapping is not a one-time exercise. Update it monthly. New permits filed. New builders entering the market. Existing builders expanding or contracting. Competitor reps changing jobs — when a competitor's trade rep leaves, their accounts are vulnerable for 60-90 days.

The rep who knows their territory better than anyone else on the floor has a structural advantage that compounds over time. While others are waiting for walk-ins, you are working a map.
